Needs changes before merge.

The holder queries read the document without changes. The new controls keep their state outside the command history. The cache tests check both unchanged and changed inputs. The body has before and after screenshots on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. I inspected the list, holder view and Recipes evidence.

## Requested before merge

1. **P3: Keep the Side preview visible on a narrow screen.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/mod.rs:193` permits a preview width below 236 px. However, `side_view.rs:43-45` reserves 216 px for dimension labels and returns when less than 20 px remains. For a 960 px viewport, `width()` selects 723.2 px. After the 170 px rail, the preview gets at most 221.3 px, even before margins and separators. Open a tool and select Side at that size: the drawing takes the early return. Switching Dimensions off does not reduce those margins. Keep enough drawing room, reduce the dimension margins, or use a different layout on narrow screens. Add a shell check that opens Side at this size. The current narrow-screen check calls only `width()`; it does not draw the editor. This finding follows from the size calculations; I did not add a test or change the code during this review.

Review fix for the finding on `3c622f8e5` (P3, the Side preview on a narrow screen). The new head is `29af2e3e1`. This commit closes that one finding. The new head waits for a fresh review.

**The fix (one rule for the whole class).** The drawing always keeps a minimum room. The dimension room gives way first:
- `side_view::margins`: with Dimensions off, the room around the drawing is an 8 px border. With Dimensions on, the room shrinks in proportion, so the drawing keeps `MIN_DRAW` (96 px), or 40 % of a wider area. The painter clips a dimension value at the edge of the area.
- `tool_library_dialog::rail_w`: on a narrow window the rail folds from 170 px to 120 px.
- `tool_library_dialog::columns`: the preview keeps 250 px while the rows keep 280 px.

I did not stack the preview under the rows. The column height is already limited by the screen, so two stacked panes each get half of it. The decision file records this.

**Tests.** Both use a 960 x 720 shell, open the tool and select Side. They read a draw counter in `side_view`, so the early return fails them.
- `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_draws_the_tool_on_a_960_px_screen`: the drawing paints with at least 96 px, the dimension lines stay on, and `rail_w` and `columns` keep their minimums.
- `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_without_dimensions_takes_their_room_on_a_960_px_screen`: with Dimensions off, the drawing paints and gets larger. No command is queued.
- Red on `3c622f8e5`: "the Side view painted no drawing (0 -> 0)". Green on `29af2e3e1`.

**Gate (macOS, head `29af2e3e1`).**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 36 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. ui lib 1630 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0. The fix does not touch `camcraft-app`.
- The branch merges cleanly with `origin/main`, so I did not merge main.
- The caches did not change. No snapshot PNG changed. The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 2. Each touched file has fewer than 310 lines.

**Screenshots** (960 x 720, headless): [Dimensions on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3897/after-side-960.png), [Dimensions off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3897/after-side-960-no-dims.png).

Ready for a re-check.

## Previous finding

1. **Fixed: the Side preview on a 960 px screen.** The previous review found one blocker on `3c622f8e55b48cc663ff370ba089b712c236ba2a`. Commit `29af2e3e167986579f18c9f704fdf41b4ef754a1` fixes it. `tool_library_dialog/mod.rs:78` reduces the rail width on a narrow window. Its `columns` function at line 86 keeps room for the preview. `tool_library_dialog/side_view.rs:86` reduces the dimension margins before the drawing loses its minimum room. Dimensions off uses an 8 px border.

Both new shell tests passed locally in UI lib:

- `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_draws_the_tool_on_a_960_px_screen`
- `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_without_dimensions_takes_their_room_on_a_960_px_screen`

These tests open Side in a 960 x 720 shell. They check the draw counter after the paint call. They also check that Dimensions off gives the drawing more room and queues no command. I read the author's response and inspected both new screenshots linked in the body. The tool is visible with Dimensions on and off. The body retains the before and after screenshots on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.

No earlier finding remains open. I found no new blocker.
